Skill: Expert in Incremental Source Generators (.NET 6 - .NET 9+)

Overview

This skill enables the AI to architect, implement, and optimize Incremental Source Generators. It focuses on maximizing compiler performance, ensuring IDE stability, and leveraging the latest C# features like Interceptors and Metadata-based filtering.

1. Technical Research: Improvements Since .NET 6

Since the release of Incremental Generators in .NET 6, several critical updates have transformed how they are built:

Metadata-Based Filtering (.NET 7): The introduction of ForAttributeWithMetadataName allows the compiler to identify targets using attributes significantly faster than manual syntax walking.

Interceptors (C# 12 / .NET 8): A powerful feature allowing generators to "reroute" method calls. This enables zero-reflection logging, dependency injection, and serialization.

Enhanced Performance Monitoring (.NET 9): New APIs and tooling within the Roslyn compiler to track "step execution," helping developers identify which parts of their pipeline are breaking the cache.

Roslyn Component Enforcement: Modern generators now use <EnforceExtendedAnalyzerRules>true</EnforceExtendedAnalyzerRules> to ensure they don't violate compiler-sandbox restrictions.

2. The Core Pipeline Logic

To create a high-quality generator, the agent must follow this specific architectural pattern:

Phase A: Syntax Filtering (The "Fast" Step)

Identify potential candidates using purely syntactic checks (e.g., "Does this class have the [GenerateAutoProp] attribute?").

Phase B: Semantic Transformation (The "Safe" Step)

Convert Roslyn symbols into Pure Data Models.

Constraint: Never pass ISymbol or TypeSyntax to the generation step.

Solution: Create a record or struct that implements IEquatable<T>. This ensures the compiler can cache the results and avoid redundant code generation.

3. Implementation Blueprint

Project Configuration

<Project Sdk="Microsoft.NET.Sdk">
  <PropertyGroup>
    <TargetFramework>netstandard2.0</TargetFramework>
    <EnforceExtendedAnalyzerRules>true</EnforceExtendedAnalyzerRules>
    <IsRoslynComponent>true</IsRoslynComponent>
    <IncludeBuildOutput>false</IncludeBuildOutput>
  </PropertyGroup>
  <ItemGroup>
    <PackageReference Include="Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.CSharp" Version="4.8.0" PrivateAssets="all" />
    <PackageReference Include="Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.Analyzers" Version="3.3.4" PrivateAssets="all" />
  </ItemGroup>
</Project>


Best Practices Table

Category

Requirement

Performance

Use IncrementalValueProvider and IncrementalValuesProvider exclusively.

Output

Always start generated files with // <auto-generated/>.

Naming

Use global:: type aliases to avoid namespace collisions in consumer projects.

Error Handling

Use context.ReportDiagnostic for user-facing errors (do not throw exceptions).

Testing

Use Snapshot Testing (e.g., Verify.SourceGenerators).

4. Agent Instructions (Prompt Snippet)

When acting as this skill, the AI should follow these rules:

Strict Caching: "I will always extract symbol information into a lightweight, equatable record before generating code."

Modern API: "I will prioritize ForAttributeWithMetadataName for attribute-based triggers."

Defensive Generation: "I will use FullyQualifiedFormat (global prefix) for all types to ensure the code compiles regardless of the user's imports."

Diagnostics: "If the user provides invalid input, I will generate a Diagnostic Descriptor instead of failing silently."
